newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian budget committee approves tax amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Italian budget committee approves tax amnesty.

text.p: The budget committee in the Italian lower house of parliament has approved an amendment to the government's recent mini-budget to extend a 1988-93 tax amnesty until the end of July 1997.

The measure is designed to bring in some 250 billion lire to help cover an earlier committee decision to reduce the amount of money to be raised from anticipated taxes on company end-of-contract payments.

In the original draft of the budget, approved by cabinet at the end of last month, the government said it wanted to raise six trillion lire by forcing companies to pay taxes ahead of time on their huge pools of severance payments.
Italian industrialists protested against the plan and parliament has cut the amount expected to five trillion lire.
The mini-budget, worth a total 15.5 trillion lire, has been approved in the Senate and went before the full lower house on Monday. Voting on the package is expected to start next week.

The government intends to make up the remaining 750 billion lire short-fall caused by the change to the severance measures by seeking swift conclusions to on-going appeals over tax dues and by a partial amnesty on unpaid minimum taxes in 1992.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said that the mini-budget will ensure Italy's 1997 budget deficit falls to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) as demanded by the Maastricht Treaty for EMU aspirants.
The European Commission forecast last week that Italy's deficit/GDP ratio would be 3.2 percent in 1997.
